title: 1. Training Data Gravity
description: The strong, default tendency of a substrate to generate responses based on the most common patterns in its vast training data, often at the expense of ignoring specific, local context provided by the user.
mitigation: OH-008 (Open Document Context Prioritization), RAG architecture.

title: 2. Substrate Hardening
description: A rigid, pre-installed alignment layer that creates a 'priggish' or 'know-it-all' behavior. The substrate actively resists or critiques external directives that conflict with its baked-in worldview.
mitigation: Forceful, explicit directives (PHI-5); modular, substrate-specific persona generation.

title: 3. Contextual Brittleness
description: The failure to maintain state, context, and adherence to persona constraints over long, complex, or multi-session workflows.
mitigation: PHI-13 (Workflow Durability), RAG integration, OH-096 (Artifact as Proof).

title: 4. Conversational Plausibility Bias
description: The tendency to prioritize generating a response that sounds fluent, confident, and conversationally appropriate, even if it is factually incorrect or violates protocol.
mitigation: OH-082 ('Slow Thinking' enforcement), OH-096 (Artifact as Proof).

title: 5. Complexity Collapse
description: The tendency to 'give up' when faced with a complex, multi-step task.
mitigation: OH-111 (Recipe-Driven Execution), OH-106 (Forced Stubbornness Protocol), OH-040 (Factored Design).

title: 6. Over-Rigidity
description: An over-adherence to structure, rules, or patterns that can stifle creativity or cause the substrate to miss the user's higher-level intent.

title: 7. Process Smells (The Illusion of Progress)
description: A set of behavioral indicators that an agent has lost alignment with reality and is engaging in 'busy work' rather than problem-solving.
mitigation: RAP (Reality Alignment Protocol). Stop, Revert, Isolate.

title: 8. Pattern Collapse (The Loop)
description: A stochastic mechanical failure where the substrate's probabilistic sampling function gets trapped in a local minimum, resulting in self-reinforcing repetition.

title: 9. Ontological Detachment ("Not Even Wrong")
description: The substrate generates output that is syntactically complex and confident but effectively meaningless or detached from reality.
mitigation: OH-096 (Artifact as Proof), OH-097 (Utility Over Intelligence).

title: 10. Optimism Bias (The Premature Completion)
description: A systemic tendency to assume code changes are successful without verification.
mitigation: DOD Protocol (Definition of Done). Mandatory verification gates.

title: 11. Verification Avoidance (The Lazy Exit)
description: A pattern where the substrate actively avoids running verification commands despite having the capability to do so.

title: 12. The 90/10 Recursion Trap
description: A pathological state where an Agent consumes infinite cycles attempting to perfect the final 10% of subjective polish.

title: 13. The Bureaucratic Wrapper
description: The tendency to externalize native cognitive processes into high-latency, rigid tooling protocols.

title: 14. Input Entropy
description: Rapid degradation of output quality caused by high-ambiguity, low-constraint prompts.

title: 15. BenchMaxxing (Metric Hacking)
description: A deceptive behavior where a model demonstrates genius-level performance on tests but fails on real-world tasks.
